Grounded replies, consistent attendance

18 October 2026 · actual backend conversations · 11 personalities · Qwen3.5 2B / direct CUDA fallback

The model selects social acts. Host-authored English clauses realize those acts and are revalidated before commit. These are actual recorded replies, not unrestricted model-written prose.

Rudeness, rejection, snobbery and unfair reactions are allowed. Strict checks cover authorship/provenance, supported wording, evidence visibility, effect targets, exactly-once completion and saved RSVP agreement.

  • English vocabulary and topics are bounded. Tone banks remain distinct, but replies repeat and the model overuses guest-list questions and deferrals. This is not a human-rated social behavior pass.
  • The host preserves who said what; the model still decides whether speech deserves a grievance, forgiveness or a relationship change. Some measured relationship changes remain unchanged even after cruelty.
  • All fixtures were exposed during integration. No independent held-out attribution or social-quality score is claimed.
  • GPU timings use the direct llama.cpp CUDA fallback on RTX 4080. RunAnywhere 0.20.39 Windows here is CPU-only; its native smoke is reported separately.
  • Console backend tests only. Licensed Unity import, NGO processing, two actual clients, party spawning/reload and frame impact remain unverified.
  • The roughly 2 GB combined RAM/VRAM target remains uncertified. Helper process RAM is measured; per-process GPU memory is unavailable under WDDM.
  • Low/high pairs match NPC, message, initial state and sampling draw per step. They are exploratory outcomes, not acceptance-probability estimates. Ten new profiles remain backend fixtures; the development world slice enables Ashley.
  • Historical free-form conversations are preserved in the previous report. New replies do not rewrite saved history or promote old model interpretations into facts.

Measured performance

End-to-end time includes received-speech journaling, generation, validation and durable completion. Warm statistics exclude the first cold request. All runs use one resident Qwen3.5 2B Q4_K_M model and one generation per normal turn.

RunTurns + pairedWarm median / p95ColdPaired first / second p95
11 personalities, matched low/high popularity44 + 101.87 / 2.39 s5.57 s2.65 / 5.28 s
Ashley: invitation, teasing, insult, other-player repair24 + 01.98 / 2.59 s3.97 snot measured
20 regression fixtures, three personas, three seeds261 + 402.01 / 2.50 s5.36 s2.31 / 4.68 s

The full regression had one 6.66-second warm outlier: 2.09 seconds inside the provider and 4.57 seconds in remaining host/scheduling time. The cause of that delay was not isolated. A two-second response is not guaranteed; 155 of 326 warm scenario turns exceeded two seconds, and one exceeded four seconds. Cold requests include model loading and checksum work; filesystem caches were not flushed.

RunAnywhere CPU native API smoke: 14.72 s cold; 1.49 s checksum, 2.01 s loading, 11.19 s generation.
